title: Neonatal jaundice: SBAs
description: Single best answer questions on classification, timing and pathway.

questions.q: A term baby is jaundiced at 18 hours of age. What is the most appropriate interpretation?
questions.explanation: Jaundice in the first 24 hours is always pathological until proven otherwise; haemolysis is the key concern.

questions.q: A 3-week-old term baby has jaundice, pale stools and dark urine. Which result is most likely?
questions.explanation: Pale stools and dark urine indicate obstructive (conjugated) jaundice, for example biliary atresia.

questions.q: Which of the following is a pre-hepatic cause of jaundice?
questions.explanation: G6PD deficiency causes haemolysis and so increased bilirubin production.
